title: Azura Insurance — seed sequence & outreach notebook
content:
Notes to self: Azura looks like a fit for a small, high-value pilot (claims triage + agent assist). They have ~1.8M customers, core stack: AWS (VPC), internal KMS, and an in-house rules engine. Regulatory scope: personal lines + small commercial in US states (CA, NY, TX are priority). Expect procurement cycles 3–4 months if we get security ok.

Quick thesis:
- Problem: claims teams are overloaded; manual first-touch triage creates backlog and inconsistent outcomes.
- Redwood value prop: reduced per-claim time, predictable latency for synchronous agent assist, private deployment option to meet Azura's KMS + audit log needs.
- Pilot scope recommendation: 6-week proof-of-value on auto-claims triage (50–250 weekly claims). Show latency, cost per inference, and quality vs baseline.

Account research (raw):
- HQ: Portland, OR. Founded 2006.
- Recent public execs: CTO = Isabel Cortez (linkedIn: /isabel-cortez-azura), Head of Digital = Marcus Weller.
- Org signals: hiring for "Claims automation" role (Job posted Nov 2025) — indicates active project.
- Tech signals: public Github for some internal data tooling, uses FastAPI microservices, Kafka pipelines.
- Regulatory: they cite SOC 2 type II on careers page. Procurement will ask for encryption at rest and audit trails.

Key stakeholders (mapping — subject to confirmation):
- Isabel Cortez (CTO) — platform + security sign-off
- Marcus Weller (Head of Digital) — product sponsor / owns agent experience
- Serena Park (Head of Claims Ops) — day-to-day stakeholder; cares about time-to-contact and SLA compliance
- Procurement: likely centralized, legal will push DPAs and SCAs

Primary use-cases to pitch (ordered):
1) Agent assist (real-time suggestions + response snippets) — win = reduced handle time, measurable latency needs (<250ms token streaming desirable).
2) First-touch triage (classify severity, suggest next steps, auto-router) — win = reduce manual triage backlog.
3) Draft correspondence (automated letter/email drafts that feed into human-in-the-loop review).

Quick numbers to call out (for initial emails):
- "Show a 20–40% reduction in claims handling time in comparable pilots." (language: "typical pilot improvement")
- Latency: we can target p95 generation latency < 300ms for short prompts on Dedicated/Private config.
- Security: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS + audit logs.

Outbound sequence (seed):
- Connect (LinkedIn): short note.
  "Hi Marcus — Mallory here at Redwood Inference. We help claims teams cut manual triage time with a low-risk pilot (private deployments or Dedicated). Curious if you’re exploring models to speed up claims routing this quarter?"

- Email 1 (intro + one-pager attach):
  Subject: "Pilot idea: cut claims triage backlog at Azura (low-risk)"
  Body bullets: who we are, quick pilot summary (6 weeks, dedicated/private, KPI = triage throughput + latency), 1–page attachment (metrics + architecture), ask: 20–30 min intro.

- Email 2 (if no reply, 4 days):
  Subject: "Two pilot options for claims (private or Dedicated)"
  Body: show short case study (anonymized insurer: 30% handle-time improvement), compliance checkpoint (SOC2 + KMS), ask for intro to Claims Ops.

- Email 3 (final nudges + calendar):
  Subject: "Quick sync? 15 min to show pilot plan + SSO/KMS flow"
  Short: propose 3 times; include link to lightweight SSO/KMS doc.

Script for 2-min cold call (to Claims Ops/Senior PM):
- Intro: "Hi Serena — Mallory at Redwood. We help claims teams reduce initial triage time with a lightweight pilot that keeps data in your VPC."
- One-sentence value: "We ran a pilot with another regional insurer and cut manual triage backlog by ~35% in 6 weeks while keeping all logs in their KMS."
- Ask: "Would you be open to a 20-min run-through next week where I can show the pilot checklist and compliance notes?"

Objection handling (prep snippets):
- "We can't put data on external GPUs": "Totally get it — we offer Private deployments and a customer-controlled VPC package. Our integration doc shows KMS/HSM flow and audit log collection; we can run a compliance call with your security team early in the process."
- "We tried an LLM vendor and outputs were garbage": "Would love to compare sample outputs. We pair prompt engineering + model variant rollouts and ship a small eval harness at the start; if quality isn't there we pause — the pilot is gated by an acceptance test you control."
- "Procurement is slow": "We can start with an NDA + technical POC without procurement for the initial technical validation (non-production data or sampled/pseudonymized set). Then move into contracting if POC metrics are good."

Email templates (snippets to copy):
- To Marcus (Head of Digital):
  "Marcus — quick intro. We’ve built low-friction pilots for claims teams (6 weeks, measurable handle-time wins). We can run inside your VPC and provide the security artifacts for procurement up front. Are you available for a 20-min intro?"

- To Isabel (CTO):
  "Isabel — Mallory from Redwood. We’ve helped platform teams keep latency predictable while lowering unit cost via batching + caching. If Azura is evaluating model-serving options, we have a brief architecture note for private deploys + KMS flows I can share."

Acceptance criteria for pilot (draft):
- Functional: model reaches X quality thresholds on triage labels (precision/recall targets) on heldout set provided by Azura.
- Operational: p95 latency < 350ms for typical prompts, cost below threshold TBD.
- Security: customer-managed KMS + audit log shipped to their Splunk/S3 bucket, SOC2 artifacts provided.
- Business: measurable reduction in manual triage backlog after 6 weeks (baseline vs pilot).

Risks / red flags:
- They use very small text fields (structured claims codes) — model gains may be smaller. Need to validate sample payloads.
- Procurement/legal will likely ask for data residency and DPIA for any PI.
- Existing vendor relationships: check if they already have a preferred inference provider (Rationale: incumbents make pilots harder).

Immediate next actions (what I will do this week):
- Pull sample job posting for "Claims automation" and send to Tess (evidence for having budget).
- Draft one-pager (attach architecture + cost estimate) — aim to finish Tue.
- Send LinkedIn connect to Marcus + short message.
- Prepare anonymized case study (ask Ravi for metrics / redaction help).

Notes to self / voice memo fragments:
- Use concrete numbers in outreach but mark as "typical pilot" to avoid overpromising.
- On calls, lead with security posture (KMS, audit, private deploy) — Azura signals are security-sensitive.
- If they push for on-prem, escalate to Solutions Eng early — on-prem needs infra scoping.

Reference links / artifacts to attach later:
- pilot-one-pager-v2.pdf (internal)
- security-kms-flow.md (internal confluence link: CONFLUENCE-azura-kms-41)
- anonymized-case-study-insurer-x.pdf

End of notebook.

-- Mallory (quick log): 2026-02-10 — reached out to Marcus on LinkedIn; no reply yet. Will send Email 1 on Mon 2026-02-16.
